title: How do we write number names as digits with commas?
description: Joseph reads six number names from a bus ticket board in Chennai. The video writes each as digits with a comma.
teaching_notes: One idea: the part before the word thousand comes first, then three digits, with zeros filling empty places. Watch for the child who writes too few digits after the comma.

source: Let Us Do 2, write the numbers
video_script.why: The child can say five digit names but needs to turn them back into digits, including names that skip places.
video_script.substitution: Write the part before the word thousand, add a comma, then write exactly three digits, filling empty places with zeros.
video_script.anchor: a bus ticket board at a stand in Chennai that Joseph reads
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu writes ninety thousand nine as nine zero comma nine. Three digits must follow the comma, so two zeros come before the nine.
video_script.payoff_line: three digits always follow the comma, so empty places are filled with zeros

final_answer.spoken: one zero comma seven four three; one zero comma zero one zero; five six comma four nine one; nine zero comma zero zero nine; two three comma two three zero; and three six comma zero zero one

maths_rules: six names: ten thousand seven hundred forty three; ten thousand ten; fifty six thousand four hundred ninety one; ninety thousand nine; twenty three thousand two hundred thirty; thirty six thousand one
10,743: part before thousand is 10, last three digits 743
90,009: 90, then 009 (nine is 9, so hundreds and tens hold zeros)
rule: exactly three digits follow the comma
slip: 90,9 has only one digit after the comma
video_script.design: Exercise: turn six names into digits. Hint: part before thousand, comma, three digits, zeros fill the gaps. Six names on a board with empty digit boxes; each number is written on the stage.
